title: Zelensky presents the Victory Plan to the Verkhovna Rada
body:
On 16 October 2024 President Volodymyr Zelensky presented Ukraine's Victory Plan in an address to the Verkhovna Rada. The Polish Centre for Eastern Studies described it as an effort to persuade the West to increase military and financial support.

The plan had five points. The first called for an immediate invitation for Ukraine to join NATO. The second called for expanding Ukraine's arms production and lifting the ban on missile strikes on military targets inside Russia. The third called for deploying a comprehensive non-nuclear strategic deterrence package in Ukraine. The fourth proposed a special agreement with Western partners on protecting and using strategic mineral resources in Ukraine. The fifth offered to deploy Ukrainian troops in place of US forces at military bases in Europe. Points two, three and four reportedly had classified annexes.

According to the Centre for Eastern Studies, Ukraine's leadership had promoted these principles for about two months, and the plan introduced no new concepts, continuing Kyiv's long-standing demands for more Western military support. The analysis linked the plan to Ukraine's peace formula, which calls for territorial integrity within internationally recognised borders and full sovereignty, and said Kyiv hoped Western support would bring Russia to the negotiating table.
